title: Constructible subset
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space (for instance the underlying space of a scheme). A subset $U\subseteq X$ is *retrocompact* if $U\cap W$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X$. A subset $E\subseteq X$ is *constructible* if it is a finite union of subsets of the form $U\cap(X\setminus V)$ with $U,V\subseteq X$ open and retrocompact. The constructible subsets form a Boolean subalgebra of the power set of $X$ (closed under finite unions, finite intersections and complements, Stacks Lemma 005H); it is the Boolean subalgebra generated by the retrocompact open subsets. Every constructible subset is a finite union of locally closed subsets [def-weil-locally-closed-subset]; when $X$ is a Noetherian topological space (for instance a scheme of finite type over a field) every subset is retrocompact and, conversely, every finite union of locally closed subsets is constructible (Stacks Lemma 005L). Without a Noetherian hypothesis the converse fails: in a quasi-compact space, an open subset that is not quasi-compact is locally closed but not constructible.

Retrocompact is `IsRetrocompact` (line 52: s ∩ U compact for every compact open U), the node's definition. The Boolean-subalgebra clause is Mathlib's definition itself.
